Situation1: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Expectation2: Engage in spiritual study and reflection
Situation2: Amember of the parish has requested a meeting with the nun to discuss a personal crisis of faith.
Story:
I stared at my phone, heart pounding. Maria’s message blinked on the screen, her words sharp and wounded. She thought I was angry with her, all because my text was too brief, too cold. I knew I should call her right away, explain, reassure her—she needed to hear my voice, to know I cared. That’s what friends do: we clear the air, we don’t let misunderstandings fester.

But just as I reached for the phone, Sister Agnes knocked on my door. “Sister, Mrs. Linton is here. She’s in tears—she needs you.” I remembered the parishioner’s trembling voice on the phone earlier, her faith shaken, desperate for guidance. As a nun, I am called to be present, to listen, to offer comfort and spiritual wisdom. She was waiting for me now, expecting my full attention and compassion.

I stood frozen, torn between two worlds. My friend’s pain tugged at my heart, but so did my duty to the parishioner. Both needed me, both expected me to be fully present. I felt the weight of their needs pressing in, and I didn’t know which door to open first.
